candidates.name: Nodular pseudolymphoma
support_spans: Mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, with open chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and without mitoses
candidates.why: The presence of mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition and lesional cells with specific characteristics are indicative of this condition.

candidates.name: Hematoma
support_spans: A woman in her 30s presented with a painful bruise on her hand
candidates.why: The initial presentation of a painful bruise is suggestive of a hematoma.

candidates.name: Nodular fasciitis
support_spans: Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, with open chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and without mitoses
candidates.why: The presence of spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid lesional cells is consistent with nodular fasciitis.

candidates.name: Nora's lesion
support_spans: Mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, with open chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and without mitoses
Immunohistochemistry: Strongly positive for CD34; negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A
candidates.why: The clinical presentation and histopathological features are consistent with Nora's lesion, a rare benign lesion characterized by a combination of fibrous, adipose, and pigmented components.

candidates.name: Hemosiderotic fibrolipomatous tumor
support_spans: Mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, with open chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and without mitoses
candidates.why: The presence of fibrous and adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition is consistent with a hemosiderotic fibrolipomatous tumor, a rare benign neoplasm.

candidates.name: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
support_spans: Mixed inflammatory infiltrate including neutrophils, histiocytes, and foamy macrophages
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, with open chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and without mitoses
contradict_spans: An ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque was noted on the dorsum of the left hand.
candidates.why: Although the clinical presentation is not typical, the histopathological features of pigmented villonodular synovitis, such as the mixed inflammatory infiltrate and spindled lesional cells, are present in this case.

candidates.why: The presence of a mixed inflammatory infiltrate including neutrophils, histiocytes, and foamy macrophages could suggest pigmented villonodular synovitis, although the location and other features are not typical for this condition.

unexplained_specific_evidence: An ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque was noted on the dorsum of the left hand.

selector.rationale: The presence of mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition and lesional cells that are spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation of an ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque on the dorsum of the hand does not match the typical presentation of pigmented villonodular synovitis, which usually affects the synovial lining of joints and tendon sheaths.

rejected.label: Hematoma
rejected.why: The persistence of the bruise and pain despite icing and resting, along with the radiographic and pathological findings, suggests a more complex lesion than a simple hematoma.

rejected.label: Nodular pseudolymphoma
rejected.why: The lack of lymphoid cells and the presence of mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Nodular fasciitis
rejected.why: The presence of mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition is not typical of nodular fasciitis, which usually consists of proliferating fibroblasts and inflammatory cells.

rejected.label: Nora's lesion
rejected.why: While Nora's lesion shares some similar features, the specific combination of clinical, radiographic, and pathological findings in this case more strongly supports the diagnosis of Hemosiderotic fibrolipomatous tumor.
